data.content_ref: inline:The target claims a 'covering principle of mutual exclusion at the frontier' guarantees that any candidate surviving the soundness critic is 'necessarily' pushed below the frontier by the relevance critic. But mutual exclusion of verdicts alone does not entail universal coverage of the candidate space: there could be candidates that fail BOTH critics (soundness flags them AND relevance flags them), which is consistent with mutual exclusion of the critics' domains yet breaks the claimed 'any candidate that survives soundness is necessarily rejected by relevance' chain. The argument conflates mutual exclusion of critic roles with exhaustive partition of all candidate outcomes, smuggling in an unsupported completeness premise.
